title: Suite Hebraique No. 4
identity: Glick's Suite Hebraique No. 4 is a six-movement work for alto saxophone and piano; the composer's chamber catalogue identifies a 1979 version and approx. 17:25 duration, while a 2008 recording runs about 19 minutes.

evidence.claim: Composer's chamber list identifies scoring, date, duration, and Dorn publication.
Apple Music recording lists six movements performed by Paul Brodie and Valerie Tryon.
Composer describes the Hebraique suites as several contrasting song/dance movements reflecting Jewish cultural life.

review_focus: Inference: six contrasting movements, including a lullaby, wedding dance, lament/cantorial chant, and circle dance, make style and character differentiation central; exact demands need score inspection.
